messages:
alex: Hey team — customer Reports: SSO users keep getting kicked to MFA prompt after successful auth. Happens in Chrome and Safari. Repro steps they shared below.

maria: Thanks — can you paste the exact flow and any logs they have? Is this only on Redwood Private or hosted?

alex: Hosted. Flow: OAuth login via Okta -> SAML assertion accepted -> redirected back to app -> get 401 from /api/auth/session -> browser shows MFA required modal. Happens intermittently, about 1 in 5 logins.

sam: Intermittent suggests a cookie/session stickiness or clock skew. Any pattern on region or time?

alex: Customer is in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. They see it mostly during morning US hours. Also said clearing cookies sometimes fixes it for a while.

jen: Can we get the session cookie attrs and the request/response headers? Might be SameSite or Secure flags getting munged by a proxy.

alex: They sent this snippet from their network team: 
```
Request: GET /api/auth/session
Cookie: __Host-redwood_session=eyJhbGci...; path=/; HttpOnly
Response: 302 -> /mfa?reason=stale_token
Set-Cookie: __Host-redwood_session=""; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure
```

maria: Hm, server is clearing the cookie as if it thinks the session invalidated. Any logs from our session service for that user id?

session-bot: session-checker: user-id 98421 — token verification failed: token-iat 1710498000, current-time 1710501605, allowed-skew 120s -> evaluated as valid. revocation-check: passed. last-activity: 1710498100.

sam: bot shows token-iat well before current time; not expired. Could be a duplicate login / device trust policy revoking previous session. Does customer enforce device trust in Okta?

alex: Yes, they enabled device_trust for some apps. They also mentioned a custom reverse-proxy in front of our private agent.

jen: Reverse-proxy could strip or re-order cookie headers. Browsers sometimes send cookies per domain rules; proxies can drop Set-Cookie in 302 if not configured. Also SameSite=None must be present for cross-site POSTs.

maria: Ask the customer to capture a HAR during a failing login and attach redwood response headers. Also confirm clock on their proxy and app instances.

alex: Customer attached HAR and this looks odd — after redirect back from Okta, there's an intermediate 307 to our backend via proxy where the cookie header is missing. 

sam: That aligns: missing cookie -> server thinks no session -> triggers MFA fallback -> issues Clear-cookie. Two hypotheses: proxy rewriting or Service Worker interfering. Any SW on their SPA?

alex: They said no service worker. Proxy config: using NGINX 1.18 with `proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_pass_request_headers on;` but they also have a `proxy_cookie_path / /;` rule.

jen: proxy_cookie_path can clobber attributes like HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite. If the proxy resets path without preserving attributes, browser may discard cookie or send differently.

maria: Good catch. Suggest them to remove proxy_cookie_path or use `proxy_cookie_flags` to preserve Secure and SameSite. Also confirm they forward `Set-Cookie` on redirects.

alex: I asked them to try a canary: remove `proxy_cookie_path` and test 50 logins. They asked for a safe repro we can run on our side.

sam: We can simulate with a local Okta SAML flow? Alternatively, craft a curl flow that follows redirects and preserves cookie headers: 
```
curl -v -L -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt 'https://app.example.com/login?provider=okta'
```
That will show where Set-Cookie is lost.

ops-oncall: Also check our session rotation logic: when user logs in from a new device, do we rotate session id and invalidate older ones? If Okta device trust triggers creation of a new session and we rotate without issuing a new persistent cookie via redirect, browser may have stale cookie.

sam: I checked code: session service rotates token on `device_trust=true` during SAML callback and issues new Set-Cookie in 302 response. If a proxy transforms or strips attributes on that 302, browser may reject the cookie.

maria: Action items for customer: 1) remove/adjust proxy_cookie_path; 2) verify `proxy_pass_header Set-Cookie` and `proxy_buffering off` for redirects; 3) test with Secure + SameSite=None present. For us: 1) add more debug logs around Set-Cookie emission on 302 for SAML callbacks; 2) add a temporary header `X-Debug-Set-Cookie: <cookieattrs>` when debug enabled so proxies can't drop it silently.

alex: Customer will test and get back. They also asked: why clearing cookies sometimes helps?

sam: Clearing removes stale cookie so when new Set-Cookie arrives it's accepted. But if proxy still strips attributes, it'll fail again.

jen: If customer can't change proxy, as a fallback we can change session flow to issue a redirect to a static content page that sets cookie via JS on same origin after SAML. But that's riskier. Keep as last resort.

maria: Noted. I'll create internal ticket SUP-1127 and assign to eng-auth. Add logs/har attachments once customer replies.

session-bot: Ticket created SUP-1127 by maria assigned_to eng-auth at 1710501640

alex: Thanks all. I'll update thread when they finish canary. :thumbsup:
